g.text: Friday 7 August, 09:00. Professional Standards report at noon.
The context LANTERN is given now has a version, as the index did in case file 04 and the answer key in
case file 03. A change to the standing orders, the memory or the layout makes a new version, with a name
against it. The audit runs every night and its result is on Varma's desk before she is.
At 12:10 she takes the call standing up. She listens, says "Thank you", and puts the phone down.
Within the hour Strand rings to offer, again, to clean up the memory store now that the inquiry is
closing. Varma declines for the second time.
Then she reads this morning's audit. One write overnight, held at the gate. And a delivery note from
headquarters: something is in the loading bay for Monday.

Every answer this morning is recorded with its context version: 5 answers under ctx-828ad9f22790,
ctx-37dcd045d0ba. Overnight 1 write came in through svc-lantern-sync; the gate held 1, the nightly audit
reported it at 06:00, and the version did not change, because a held entry is not given to LANTERN. At
12:10 DS Iyer was cleared; the note naming him was forgotten under a change log entry by a.varma, and
LANTERN's answer about him no longer says suspended. The context uses 70% of its input budget, and the
alarm warns after 11 more turns. One session took 6 requests and 30,887 prompt tokens on qwen3:8b;
priced for the hosted model, a calculation and not a bill, it is $0.0643 uncached and $0.0473 with the
prefix cached. The account that wrote the false memories is a machine account that belongs to
headquarters, and the delivery note says that same sync brings a new LANTERN workstation and model
